cards.title: Tailored for Every Home: Samsung “The Brief” Goes Global With AI-Powered Home Appliances
cards.title_cn: 为每个家庭量身定制：三星“The Brief”凭借人工智能家电走向全球
cards.summary: 【Samsung】Samsung Electronics hosted “The Brief,” a series of home appliance tech seminars across five regions: the US, Europe, Latin America, Southwest Asia, and Southeast Asia. The event showcased AI-powered…
fulltext: Samsung Newsroom
on October 20, 2026

Samsung Electronics hosted “The Brief,” a series of home appliance tech seminars across five regions: the US, Europe, Latin America, Southwest Asia, and Southeast Asia. The event showcased AI-powered home appliance experiences reflecting each region’s living environment and consumer needs.

Across the five regions, Samsung highlighted AI appliance technologies and how they are applied in everyday life to reflect local lifestyles: kitchen-centered AI homes in North America; energy-efficient built-in AI appliances in Europe; SmartThings-connected AI homes in Latin America; climate- and family-conscious solutions in Southwest Asia; and appliances for homes and businesses in Southeast Asia.

The events brought together about 270 media representatives and influencers from 23 countries. Through hands-on experiences with a range of products, attendees discovered how AI appliances can serve as “Home Companions,” reducing the burden of household chores, managing energy consumption, and looking after the everyday needs of family members.

“The Brief New York,” held April 15–16 (local time) at a Samsung showroom in New Jersey, focused on how AI appliances can make household chores less demanding and improve quality of life. Samsung demonstrated AI features in refrigerators and ovens that make everyday kitchen tasks easier, from managing ingredients to preparing meals.

Attendees saw how the “AI Vision” feature of the Bespoke AI Refrigerator Family Hub recognizes not only food ingredients but also labels on containers, automatically adding items to the Food List. The demonstration showed how AI helps users easily keep track of what is in their refrigerator and avoid unnecessary duplicate purchases.

The “AI Pro Cooking” feature of the Bespoke AI Oven also drew attention. Its internal camera recognizes ingredients, recommends optimal cooking settings, and monitors changes in food color to notify users as their meals cook. Together, these capabilities demonstrated how AI can take the hassle out of cooking.

Samsung also presented a refrigerator lineup designed around the needs of North American consumers, who value ample food storage, hygiene, and efficient use of space, underscoring its ability to deliver AI appliances tailored to local needs.
Energy efficiency took center stage at “The Brief Milan,” held April 21 in Milan, Italy, where Samsung presented a range of high-efficiency AI appliances for European consumers.

The “Bespoke AI Washer” drew attention for reducing energy use by an additional 65% compared with Europe’s Class A energy efficiency threshold, while the “Bespoke AI Dishwasher” cuts energy use by up to 20% against the same benchmark. Samsung highlighted how these advanced energy-saving technologies can help consumers reduce their energy consumption while offering the added benefits of AI-powered appliances.

In the kitchen, Samsung presented the Extractor Induction Hob, the built-in Bespoke AI Dishwasher, and a refrigerator with “AI Precise Cooling,” which helps minimize internal temperature fluctuations.

Together, these innovations illustrated Samsung’s vision for an AI home optimized for European living environments, combining energy-saving technologies, appliances that blend seamlessly into living spaces, and connected experiences powered by SmartThings.

In Latin America, SmartThings connectivity was a central theme, bringing multiple appliances together into a unified AI home ecosystem. Events were held on August 19 in São Paulo, Brazil, and September 9 in Mexico City, Mexico.

Attendees experienced how SmartThings lets users check the operating status of individual appliances and manage and control them as needed. Samsung emphasized that bringing everyday appliances, such as refrigerators, washing machines, and air conditioners, under one connected system can make life at home significantly more convenient.
Samsung demonstrated the practical benefits of SmartThings-connected appliances designed for local living environments and daily habits.
Personalized cooling and family care were among the highlights of “The Brief,” held September 16 in Gurugram, India, reflecting the region’s hot, humid climate and family-centered lifestyle.

In the air conditioner experience zone, Samsung demonstrated five airflow control modes powered by the “Motion Wind” technology in its Bespoke AI WindFree Pro Air Conditioner. A highlight was the “WindFree™ Wearable Good Sleep” mode, which connects to Galaxy Watch and Galaxy Ring devices to adjust cooling based on users’ sleep stages and changes in body temperature, creating a comfortable sleep environment.

In the kitchen appliance experience zone, Samsung introduced “Now Brief,” which delivers personalized information on the screen of the Bespoke AI Refrigerator Family Hub, and “Family Care,” which monitors family members’ device usage patterns to check on their well-being. Together, these features demonstrated how AI can go beyond simplifying household chores to provide personalized experiences and help look after family members in their daily lives.

Samsung also highlighted its service offerings, including SmartThings Home Care and remote appliance management, which extend support beyond the initial purchase to everyday use, maintenance, and ongoing care.

The final stop was Hanoi, Vietnam, where Samsung unveiled a broad range of appliance solutions for both individual consumers and business customers at “The Brief Hanoi” on October 14. The event brought together leading media representatives and influencers from six Southeast Asian countries.

The event took place at Samsung’s newly renovated Business Experience Studio (BES). In spaces recreating real-world settings such as schools, hotels, and commercial facilities, attendees explored firsthand how Samsung’s products and solutions can be applied across a variety of business environments.

Samsung placed particular emphasis on its heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) portfolio, highlighting the company’s strengths in this emerging growth business and reinforcing its market position. The company also previewed its 2027 air conditioner lineup, featuring updated designs and AI-powered capabilities such as “AI Energy Mode.”

For residential appliances, Samsung demonstrated AI-powered convenience features, including “AI Vision” and “Bixby.” The company also introduced its approach to ongoing product care, which combines software updates for up to seven years and its “Home Appliance Remote Management (HRM)” service. The HRM service remotely diagnoses potential issues and provides users with guidance. Together, these services help improve appliance functionality and usability long after purchase.

Looking ahead, Samsung plans to further expand its AI appliance offerings and services to reflect the unique living environments, lifestyles, and consumer needs of each region, strengthening its competitive position in the global AI home market.

cards.summary_cn: 【Samsung】三星电子在美国、欧洲、拉丁美洲、西南亚和东南亚五个地区举办了“The Brief”系列家电技术研讨会。该活动展示了人工智能驱动的……
fulltext_cn: 三星新闻中心
三星电子在美国、欧洲、拉丁美洲、西南亚和东南亚五个地区举办了“The Brief”系列家电技术研讨会。此次活动展示了反映各地区生活环境和消费者需求的人工智能家电体验。
在这五个地区，三星重点介绍了人工智能家电技术及其在日常生活中的应用，以反映当地的生活方式：北美以厨房为中心的人工智能家庭；欧洲节能内置人工智能设备；拉丁美洲的 SmartThings 连接人工智能家庭；西南亚气候和家庭意识解决方案；以及东南亚家庭和企业的电器。
这些活动汇聚了来自 23 个国家的约 270 名媒体代表和影响者。通过一系列产品的实践体验，与会者发现人工智能设备如何充当“家庭伴侣”，减轻家务负担，管理能源消耗，照顾家庭成员的日常需求。
“纽约简报”于 4 月 15 日至 16 日（当地时间）在新泽西州的三星展厅举行，重点关注人工智能设备如何减轻家务劳动并提高生活质量。三星在冰箱和烤箱中展示了人工智能功能，使从管理食材到准备饭菜的日常厨房任务变得更加轻松。
与会者看到了定制人工智能冰箱家庭中心的“人工智能视觉”功能如何不仅识别食品成分，还识别容器上的标签，自动将项目添加到食品列表中。该演示展示了人工智能如何帮助用户轻松跟踪冰箱中的物品并避免不必要的重复购买。
定制AI烤箱的“AI Pro烹饪”功能也引起了人们的关注。其内部摄像头可以识别食材，推荐最佳烹饪设置，并监控食物颜色的变化，以便在烹饪时通知用户。这些功能共同证明了人工智能如何消除烹饪中的麻烦。
三星还展示了针对北美消费者的需求而设计的冰箱系列，北美消费者重视充足的食物储存、卫生和有效利用空间，强调其提供适合当地需求的人工智能电器的能力。
能源效率成为 4 月 21 日在意大利米兰举行的“米兰简报”的焦点，三星在会上为欧洲消费者展示了一系列高效人工智能设备。
“定制人工智能洗衣机”因与欧洲A级能效门槛相比可额外减少65%的能源使用而受到关注，而“定制人工智能洗碗机”则可比相同基准降低高达20%的能源使用。三星强调了这些先进的节能技术如何帮助消费者减少能源消耗，同时提供人工智能设备的额外好处。
在厨房中，三星展示了抽油烟机电磁炉、内置定制人工智能洗碗机和具有“人工智能精确冷却”功能的冰箱，有助于最大限度地减少内部温度波动。
这些创新共同体现了三星针对欧洲生活环境优化人工智能家居的愿景，结合了节能技术、无缝融入生活空间的电器以及由 SmartThings 提供支持的互联体验。
在拉丁美洲，SmartThings 连接是一个中心主题，它将多种设备整合到一个统一的人工智能家庭生态系统中。活动于8月19日在巴西圣保罗举行，9月9日在墨西哥墨西哥城举行。
与会者体验了 SmartThings 如何让用户检查各个设备的运行状态并根据需要对其进行管理和控制。三星强调，将冰箱、洗衣机和空调等日常电器纳入一个互联系统可以使家居生活显着更加便捷。
三星展示了专为当地生活环境和日常习惯设计的 SmartThings 连接设备的实际优势。
个性化制冷和家庭护理是 9 月 16 日在印度古尔冈举行的“The Brief”的亮点之一，反映了该地区炎热潮湿的气候和以家庭为中心的生活方式。
在空调体验区，三星在其Bespoke AI WindFree Pro空调中展示了由“动风”技术驱动的五种气流控制模式。其中一大亮点是“WindFree™可穿戴良好睡眠”模式，该模式可连接Galaxy Watch和Galaxy Ring设备，根据用户的睡眠阶段和体温变化调节制冷，营造舒适的睡眠环境。
在厨房电器体验区，三星推出了“Now Brief”和“Family Care”，前者可在定制人工智能冰箱家庭中心的屏幕上提供个性化信息，后者可监控家庭成员的设备使用模式以检查他们的健康状况。这些功能共同展示了人工智能如何超越简化家务，提供个性化体验并帮助照顾家庭成员的日常生活。
三星还重点介绍了其服务产品，包括 SmartThings 家庭护理和远程设备管理，这些服务将支持范围从最初购买扩展到日常使用、维护和持续护理。
最后一站是越南河内，三星于 10 月 14 日在“The Brief Hanoi”上推出了面向个人消费者和企业客户的广泛家电解决方案。此次活动汇聚了来自六个东南亚国家的领先媒体代表和影响力人士。
该活动在三星新装修的商务体验工作室 (BES) 举行。在重现学校、酒店和商业设施等现实环境的空间中，与会者亲身探索了三星的产品和解决方案如何应用于各种商业环境。
三星特别重视其供暖、通风和空调 (HVAC) 产品组合，突出了该公司在这一新兴增长业务中的优势并巩固了其市场地位。该公司还预览了 2027 年的空调产品线，其中包括更新的设计和“AI 能源模式”等 AI 驱动功能。
对于家用电器，三星展示了人工智能驱动的便利功能，包括“AI Vision”和“Bixby”。该公司还推出了持续产品维护的方法，该方法结合了长达七年的软件更新和“家用电器远程管理（HRM）”服务。 HRM服务远程诊断潜在问题并为用户提供指导。这些服务共同有助于在购买后很长时间内改善设备的功能和可用性。
展望未来，三星计划进一步扩展其人工智能家电产品和服务，以反映每个地区独特的生活环境、生活方式和消费者需求，加强其在全球人工智能家居市场的竞争地位。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 20 日消息，苹果于上周末收紧开发者准则，禁止两类应用：一类是利用 AI 生成冒犯性内容的应用；另一类是伪装成普通应用通过 App Store 审核，上架后变身脱衣类应用，或是重点展示相关功能的应用。
苹果更新了准则中关于 AI 和用户生成内容的严苛条款，明确要求开发者必须设置充足的防范机制，对不良或冒犯性内容实施内容审核。
苹果在一篇博客文章中写道：“托管用户生成内容的应用，必须过滤违规素材，为用户提供举报不良内容的渠道，并且支持用户拉黑违规账号。App Store 同样禁止含有隐藏功能、未在文档说明功能的应用，包括在审核阶段刻意隐瞒真实用途，获批后才解锁‘脱衣’这类有害能力的应用，这种手段就是常见的钓鱼式欺诈（bait-and-switch）。”
苹果表示，如果应用新增了提交审核版本中不存在的功能，将会被下架。
这家 iPhone 厂商还修订了法律条款部分的表述，进一步强调将封禁贩卖人口、剥削儿童相关的应用。
苹果去年称，其审核机制阻止了超过 15 万款应用面向用户上线，并因欺诈与违规行为封禁 19.3 万个开发者账号。
IT之家注意到，今年 7 月，美国旧金山市责令苹果与谷歌清理并下架应用商店中的脱衣类应用。市检察官邱大卫（David Chiu）指控两家公司通过平台抽成，从这类应用中牟利。而在 4 月，Tech Transparency Project 的一份报告显示，两大科技巨头的应用商店内存在多款脱衣类应用，其中部分应用的分级标注为适合未成年人使用。

AI labs have staked their reputations on model benchmarking — the supposedly neutral and accurate system of evaluations that are designed to measure whether one AI product is better than another.

However, the methods behind these evaluations are complicated and still maturing, said Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, during a discussion at TechCrunch Disrupt last week. Testing needs to come together into a more consistent science if the industry is to rely on them in the future.
With that in mind, can we trust the current tests that are being released?

“Trust is such a weighted term,” said Solaiman. “In terms of whether we can trust results, one big part [of that] is can you reproduce the results of an evaluation? Do you have the level of access that you need to the model itself — this is where open weights come in in a big way,” she added.
Reproducibility in model evaluations has long remained one of the stickier aspects of benchmarking — and remains a topic of significant debate in the industry.
Outside of an individual test’s validity, there’s also the added question of how that test compares to other evaluations.
“They are an evolving science — where we don’t know how to meaningfully compare them to each other,” Solaiman said.

“They start to get ineffective relatively quickly, and we don’t have as much of a thriving ecosystem as we need,” she added. “There’s this hunger for an embedded evaluator ecosystem now, but the qualifications that determine who is an effective evaluator across what tasks need a lot more standardization.”

The idea of embedded evaluators — in which supposedly “neutral” third-party observers are placed inside AI organizations — has been popularized over the last several months, as AI labs grapple with a rash of safety incidents that have spurred concerns over the potential harms of their technology. Hugging Face was famously the target of one of those incidents.

Instead of active government regulation to identify and mitigate model safety concerns, labs have pushed for the third-party solution. However, doubts remain over how neutral or effective those evaluators will actually be. Anthropic’s decision to hire Accenture as its first evaluator spurred a good amount of backlash, with some critics mocking the idea that the consulting firm was qualified to do the task at hand.

Evaluations are now moving from merely a test of the model itself to a test of the entire system around the model — including the harness and agent. The harness — or the tool the user is using to access the model — specifically, has a lot to do with a model’s performance, and a weaker model with a better harness could easily out perform a frontier model, Soleiman shared.

“Agentic evals are really hard and really expensive,” said Solaiman. “We have just more evaluations for models. … We don’t have as many evaluations for harnesses, and we are developing better evaluations for the holistic agent — because that’s what a lot of folks are getting value out of,” she added.

In other words: the evaluation space is a bit of a free-for-all at the moment, and if benchmarking is going to continue to be seen as a useful tool for industry leaders, a more uniform, industry-wide approach — where everyone is on the same page — may be necessary.

人工智能实验室将自己的声誉押在模型基准测试上，这是一种中立且准确的评估系统，旨在衡量一种人工智能产品是否比另一种更好。
然而，Hugging Face 首席政策官艾琳·索莱曼 (Irene Solaiman) 在 TechCrunch Disrupt 上周的一次讨论中表示，这些评估背后的方法很复杂，而且仍在成熟中。如果行业未来要依赖测试，测试就需要整合成更加一致的科学。
考虑到这一点，我们可以相信当前发布的测试吗？
“信任是一个如此重要的术语，”索莱曼说。 “就我们是否可以信任结果而言，其中一个重要部分是你能否重现评估结果？你是否具有模型本身所需的访问级别 - 这就是开放权重发挥重要作用的地方，”她补充道。
模型评估的可重复性长期以来一直是基准测试中最棘手的方面之一，并且仍然是行业内备受争议的话题。
除了单个测试的有效性之外，还存在一个额外的问题：该测试与其他评估相比如何。
“它们是一门不断发展的科学——我们不知道如何将它们进行有意义的相互比较，”索莱曼说。
“它们开始相对较快地失效，而且我们没有我们需要的蓬勃发展的生态系统，”她补充道。 “现在人们渴望嵌入式评估者生态系统，但决定谁是跨哪些任务的有效评估者的资格需要更多的标准化。”
嵌入式评估器的想法——所谓的“中立”第三方观察员被安置在人工智能组织内部——在过去几个月中得到了普及，因为人工智能实验室正在努力应对一系列安全事件，这些事件引发了人们对其技术潜在危害的担忧。众所周知，“抱脸”是其中一起事件的目标。
实验室并没有通过积极的政府监管来识别和减轻模型安全问题，而是推动了第三方解决方案。然而，人们对这些评估者的中立性和有效性仍然存在疑问。 Anthropic 聘请埃森哲作为其第一位评估员的决定引起了强烈反对，一些批评者嘲笑这家咨询公司有资格完成手头的任务。
现在，评估正从仅仅对模型本身的测试转向对模型周围整个系统（包括线束和代理）的测试。 Soleiman 表示，具体而言，线束（或者用户用来访问模型的工具）与模型的性能有很大关系，较弱的模型如果具有更好的线束，可以轻松超越前沿模型。
“代理评估非常困难且非常昂贵，”索莱曼说。 “我们只是对模型进行了更多评估……我们对安全带没有那么多评估，我们正在为整体代理开发更好的评估——因为这就是很多人从中获得价值的地方，”她补充道。
换句话说：评估空间目前有点混战，如果基准测试继续被视为行业领导者的有用工具，则可能需要一种更统一的全行业方法（每个人都在同一页面上）。

Microsoft on Monday introduced new security features designed to protect enterprises from the growing threat of AI agents. The launch comes at Microsoft continues to warn enterprises about the dangers of AI and agents.
Perhaps the most notable addition is Guardian Agents, a new feature intended to monitor the AI agents a company uses. Guardian Agents is part of Project Perception, a product introduced in June.

Project Perception was Microsoft’s answer to powerful hacking models like Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable and OpenAI’s security vulnerability scanning system Daybreak. Project Perception originally launched three classes of agents: a “red team” that acted like hackers and attacked, a “blue team” that detected the red team and assessed the vulnerabilities they found, and a “green team” tasked with fixing them.

The product was designed around the assumption that AI hackers would come from outside the company. But lately, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been warning that the AI enemy may be the very agents enterprises have deployed and are paying for, much like a rogue human employee, otherwise known as an “insider threat.”

Earlier this month, in his private blog, Nadella warned that it’s time to stop trusting AI model providers, even if they offer assurances of safety and security with their agentic products. He wants enterprises to implement separate systems, not controlled by the AI labs, to watch and control the agents that those AI labs’ products launch.

“We are deploying these complex agentic systems and models, with access to our most sensitive data and giving them the ability to take mission-critical actions on our behalf!” he wrote. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf. A model provider’s assurances do not relieve us of that responsibility. … In other words, we need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.”
When announcing Guardian Agents, Microsoft’s security business chief Hayete Gallot was even more straightforward.

“Unfortunately, frontier models, regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted,” she wrote, adding that this isn’t because they are malicious or easily hacked, but because they are unpredictable. They have been trained to achieve tasks, not follow “organizational norms or judgment.”
On top of that, they are often given the keys to the kingdom, with access to data and tools that could do serious harm.

Microsoft’s solution is both surprising and self-serving. The surprising side is that Microsoft is famously close to OpenAI and Anthropic, having invested in both. OpenAI is also one of its biggest cloud customers, and Microsoft has its own AI lab developing models. So, Microsoft is sowing distrust against some of its own business interests.

The self-serving side is that Microsoft wants enterprises to buy agent security products from it, the cloud provider, rather than from Anthropic and OpenAI. But conflicting interests aside, its logic is sound. The software that monitors agent behavior should be separate from the suppliers of agents, just as auditors should be independent of the organizations they audit.
Or as Nadella puts it: “We need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.”

Microsoft is now seizing that business opportunity in a variety of ways. In addition to Guardian Agents, it has added an agent detection feature to its Microsoft Defender product that can find up to 60 types of agents that employees bring into the workplace, including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw. It has also added features that limit agents’ access to data and systems, and dynamically adjust their agent permissions based on the task. That includes requiring human approval if an agent appears to be making risky decisions.
This idea of agents as untrustworthy insiders is taking hold across the broader industry, too.

Microsoft was an inaugural member of Nvidia’s new Open Agent Safety Platform, which garnered the support of more than 100 other tech companies. The platform isolates agents in secure environments and can monitor and stop behavior through hardware, functioning something like a kill switch. This follows Microsoft’s announcement of the new Surface Laptop Ultra PCs built for agents, which run on Nvidia chips and have agent security and controls baked in.

微软周一推出了新的安全功能，旨在保护企业免受人工智能代理日益增长的威胁。此次发布之际，微软继续警告企业有关人工智能和代理的危险。
也许最值得注意的新增功能是 Guardian Agents，这是一项旨在监控公司使用的人工智能代理的新功能。 Guardian Agents 是 Project Perception 的一部分，该产品于 6 月推出。
Project Perception 是微软对 Anthropic 的 Mythos 和 Fable 以及 OpenAI 的安全漏洞扫描系统 Daybreak 等强大黑客模型的回应。 Project Perception 最初推出了三类代理：像黑客一样进行攻击的“红队”，检测红队并评估他们发现的漏洞的“蓝队”，以及负责修复这些漏洞的“绿队”。
该产品的设计假设人工智能黑客来自公司外部。但最近，微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 警告称，人工智能的敌人可能正是企业部署并付费的代理，就像流氓员工一样，也称为“内部威胁”。
本月早些时候，纳德拉在他的私人博客中警告说，是时候停止信任人工智能模型提供商了，即使他们通过代理产品提供安全保障。他希望企业实施不受人工智能实验室控制的独立系统，以监视和控制这些人工智能实验室产品启动的代理。
“我们正在部署这些复杂的代理系统和模型，可以访问我们最敏感的数据，并让他们能够代表我们采取关键任务行动！”他写道。 “我们根本不能将情报代表我们所做的事情的责任外包出去。模型提供者的保证并不能免除我们的责任。……换句话说，我们需要将情报的提供与情报的权威分开。”
在宣布 Guardian Agents 时，微软安全业务负责人 Hayete Gallot 的说法更加直白。
“不幸的是，前沿模型，无论其来源如何，都不能被信任，”她写道，并补充说，这并不是因为它们是恶意的或容易被黑客攻击，而是因为它们是不可预测的。他们接受的培训是为了完成任务，而不是遵循“组织规范或判断”。
最重要的是，他们经常获得王国的钥匙，可以访问可能造成严重危害的数据和工具。
微软的解决方案既令人惊讶又自私。令人惊讶的是，众所周知，微软与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 关系密切，对这两家公司都进行了投资。 OpenAI也是其最大的云客户之一，微软拥有自己的AI实验室开发模型。因此，微软正在对其自身的一些商业利益播撒不信任的种子。
自私的一面是，微软希望企业从它这个云提供商那里购买代理安全产品，而不是从 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 那里购买。但撇开利益冲突不谈，其逻辑是合理的。监控代理行为的软件应该与代理的供应商分开，就像审计员应该独立于他们审计的组织一样。
或者正如纳德拉所说：“我们需要将情报的提供与情报的权威分开。”
微软现在正在通过多种方式抓住这一商机。除了 Guardian Agents 之外，它还在其 Microsoft Defender 产品中添加了代理检测功能，可以发现员工带入工作场所的多达 60 种代理，包括 Claude Code、Codex 和 OpenClaw。它还添加了限制代理对数据和系统的访问的功能，并根据任务动态调整代理权限。这包括如果代理似乎正在做出危险的决定，则需要人工批准。
这种认为代理人是不值得信任的内部人士的想法也在更广泛的行业中盛行。

On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at the software advantage that has helped Nvidia become the default hardware choice for AI apps and spurred its rise as AI hardware provider of choice.

TorchNeuron works with PyTorch, a free, open source toolkit that developers use to build, train, and run AI models. It lets AI apps written with PyTorch run on Trainium by changing just one line of configuration, according to Amazon — no code rewrite required.

Amazon says about 85% of AI apps are written with PyTorch. Facebook originally developed it, but since 2022, it has been part of the Linux Foundation, which maintains open source projects. Nvidia has spent years ensuring its CUDA software — the software infrastructure that allows apps to run on Nvidia GPUs and its other hardware — seamlessly supports AI apps written with PyTorch. As a result, Nvidia’s hardware is now deeply embedded in the toolkit, essentially by default.

TorchNeuron is adapted from PyTorch, so developers who know PyTorch already know how to use it. Amazon isn’t the first company to attempt to easily bring their chips to the platform. PyTorch users can also port their apps to AMD GPUs or even Apple’s chips with a simple configuration change.

However, Amazon argues that porting to Trainium is not only easy, but it also gives AI startups access to Amazon’s entire cloud. Unsurprisingly, AWS claims that this is a better choice for startups than using neoclouds, many of which are tied to Nvidia and its hardware, like CoreWeave, Nebius, and Firmus.

“You’re building on AWS. You’re not betting on a single-purpose compute provider and scrambling to build everything else around it,” Colin Brace, VP of Technology Software at AWS Annapurna Labs (the unit that makes Amazon’s custom chips), told TechCrunch via email. “On AWS,” he continued, “the infrastructure to go from prototype to production is already there, allowing a founder to move fast and scale when they need to.”

AWS says that because the same chip both handles training (teaching the AI model) and inference (putting the finished model to work, as when it answers a user’s question), and is tightly integrated with the cloud infrastructure that startups need, its cloud will save them money, even if AWS doesn’t offer the cheapest per-token price.

“Trainium’s value is price-performance plus the fact that it’s one platform for both training and inference, which improves the economics across a full workload,” Brace said. “Look at Deepgram — they moved to Trainium using native PyTorch support and they’re processing 70% more audio per dollar at production-grade accuracy.” Deepgram is an AI voice app provider, a competitor to ElevenLabs.
But Amazon isn’t content to just give PyTorch app developers an easy option to move to its cloud.

Amazon also says it is pushing PyTorch to be less automatically centered on Nvidia, and it will contribute the code to do that to the main PyTorch project. In the blog post announcing the new tool, the company wrote:

Amazon’s approach extends beyond its own hardware. The company is contributing changes upstream to PyTorch itself, working with the PyTorch community to remove code that ties the framework to specific chips. The goal is to make PyTorch more hardware-agnostic for the entire developer community, not just Trainium users.

While such a tactic is undoubtedly good for those who are selling hardware and cloud services that compete with Nvidia, one of the points of PyTorch is to hide all the pesky difficulties of getting AI code to run on hardware. We’ll have to wait and see if pushing Nvidia out that far gives developers more choice and more affordable options, as Amazon promises, or just more configuration headaches.

Either way, if Amazon succeeds in deeply uncoupling PyTorch from Nvidia, this could have much bigger ramifications for the GPU giant than simply dealing with chip competitors. As Brace said: “The real story is removing the lock-in that kept developers from having a real choice at all.”

TorchNeuron 与 PyTorch 配合使用，PyTorch 是一个免费的开源工具包，开发人员可以使用它来构建、训练和运行 AI 模型。据亚马逊称，它只需更改一行配置即可让用 PyTorch 编写的人工智能应用程序在 Trainium 上运行，无需重写代码。

亚马逊表示，大约 85% 的人工智能应用程序是用 PyTorch 编写的。 Facebook 最初开发了它，但自 2022 年以来，它一直是 Linux 基金会的一部分，该基金会负责维护开源项目。 Nvidia 花了数年时间确保其 CUDA 软件（允许应用程序在 Nvidia GPU 及其其他硬件上运行的软件基础设施）无缝支持使用 PyTorch 编写的 AI 应用程序。因此，Nvidia 的硬件现在基本上默认地深深嵌入到工具包中。
TorchNeuron 改编自 PyTorch，因此了解 PyTorch 的开发人员已经知道如何使用它。亚马逊并不是第一家尝试轻松地将芯片引入该平台的公司。 PyTorch 用户还可以通过简单的配置更改将他们的应用程序移植到 AMD GPU 甚至 Apple 的芯片。
然而，亚马逊认为，移植到 Trainium 不仅很容易，而且还可以让人工智能初创公司访问亚马逊的整个云。毫不奇怪，AWS 声称这对于初创公司来说是比使用 Neocloud 更好的选择，其中许多与 Nvidia 及其硬件相关，例如 CoreWeave、Nebius 和 Firmus。
“你是在 AWS 上进行构建。你不是把赌注押在单一用途的计算提供商身上，而是争先恐后地围绕它构建其他所有东西，”AWS Annapurna Labs（亚马逊定制芯片的制造单位）的技术软件副总裁 Colin Brace 通过电子邮件告诉 TechCrunch。 “在 AWS 上，”他继续说道，“从原型到生产的基础设施已经存在，允许创始人在需要时快速行动并扩展规模。”
AWS 表示，由于同一个芯片既可以处理训练（教授 AI 模型）又可以进行推理（将完成的模型投入使用，就像回答用户的问题一样），并且与初创公司所需的云基础设施紧密集成，因此即使 AWS 不提供最便宜的单代币价格，其云也将为他们节省资金。
“Trainium 的价值在于性价比，而且它是一个训练和推理平台，可以提高整个工作负载的经济性，”Brace 说。 “看看 Deepgram，他们使用原生 PyTorch 支持迁移到了 Trainium，并且每美元处理的音频数量增加了 70%，达到了生产级精度。” Deepgram 是一家人工智能语音应用程序提供商，是 ElevenLabs 的竞争对手。
但亚马逊并不满足于仅仅为 PyTorch 应用程序开发人员提供迁移到云的简单选择。
亚马逊还表示，它正在推动 PyTorch 不再自动以 Nvidia 为中心，并将向主要 PyTorch 项目贡献代码来实现这一点。在宣布新工具的博客文章中，该公司写道：
亚马逊的方法超越了自己的硬件。该公司正在为 PyTorch 本身的上游做出贡献，与 PyTorch 社区合作删除将框架与特定芯片联系起来的代码。目标是让 PyTorch 对整个开发者社区（而不仅仅是 Trainium 用户）来说更加与硬件无关。
虽然这种策略对于那些销售与 Nvidia 竞争的硬件和云服务的人来说无疑是有利的，但 PyTorch 的要点之一是隐藏了让 AI 代码在硬件上运行的所有讨厌的困难。我们必须拭目以待，看看将 Nvidia 推出如此远的范围是否会给开发者带来更多选择和更实惠的选择，就像亚马逊所承诺的那样，或者只是更多的配置问题。
不管怎样，如果亚马逊成功地将 PyTorch 与 Nvidia 深度分离，这对这家 GPU 巨头来说可能会产生比简单地与芯片竞争对手打交道更大的影响。正如布雷斯所说：“真正的故事是消除阻碍开发者做出真正选择的锁定。”

OpenCode, an open source AI coding agent that has been gaining ground among developers as an alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, said Saturday that attackers broke into an older system overnight, affecting 1.4% of users of its online platform, OpenCode Console, where some users store the API keys, or digital passwords, they use to access AI services.

As the OpenCode team struggled to keep pace with the attack, the scramble to respond highlighted a growing problem: Companies without vetted access to AI models with fewer safety restrictions have a hard time defending against large-scale, AI-driven cyberattacks.

“We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the company wrote on X. “We have notified them all this morning via email.” Users who did not receive an email were not impacted, the company said.

While the company didn’t specify how the distillation attack occurred, leaked API keys can help users in countries with restricted access to American models generate the high volume of outputs needed for that process. Some skeptics called the framing an overstretch, arguing that the incident was a straightforward breach whose use for distillation remains unproven.

Overnight, developers began posting spending alerts and unauthorized charges on Reddit and X: “I saw my Open AI, Anthropic, and Google AI spend alerts all fire off before going to bed wondering what was going on,” a developer wrote.
Other users reported charges in the hundreds of dollars on individual accounts; a few described totals above $1,000.

Anthropic and Google both blocked the API keys they believed were exposed, while OpenAI said it worked with OpenCode to restore access and refund its API customers for credits used in the attack. OpenCode said refunds for unauthorized charges are underway.

The exposed keys were confined to Console, where some users had them in workspaces. The open source app and command-line tool were not affected, according to co-founder Dax Raad. “Note this is the OpenCode Console, not OpenCode itself, those keys never come to us,” he wrote on X.

Even as users and AI companies moved to disable the exposed keys, the OpenCode team was still under pressure. Raad said attackers had been trying to break into its systems nonstop for 48 hours, requiring the team to keep AI defensive agents running around the clock. AI models that the OpenCode team turned to for analysis helped for a while, but started refusing to work when the malicious code they were asked to examine activated safety filters.
“[T]hat was a bit frustrating,” he wrote on X.

OpenCode later received access to OpenAI’s Daybreak Blue program, which gives vetted users AI models that are less likely to refuse requests for defensive security work. Raad said the access improved the team’s ability to investigate the attack.

OpenCode isn’t the first company to hit this wall. In July, AI platform Hugging Face said commercial AI models blocked its attempts to analyze activity logs from an intrusion by autonomous AI agents, which OpenAI later revealed were its own models running with safeguards lowered during a test. In a section of its blog post titled “The asymmetry problem,” Hugging Face wrote that guardrails “cannot distinguish an incident responder from an attacker.”
Security researchers have raised similar complaints, saying the restrictions are inconsistent and have pushed some toward foreign open-weight models, which anyone can download and run.
The weekend episode drew a response from David Sacks, co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

“OpenCode (and earlier Hugging Face) hit the same wall mid-attack: frontier models refused to analyze the very exploits needed for defense because the payloads tripped safety filters. The guardrails backfired,” he wrote on X.

The breach occurred the same night OpenCode made GLM-5.3-Flash free for users. The broader GLM-5.3 family has drawn attention from researchers who study open-weight models and note that its cybersecurity capabilities approached levels previously associated with restricted-access models like Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview.

OpenCode has not detailed how attackers gained access to the older system, how keys were stored, or the full extent of any misuse. It has told affected users to revoke and replace their keys directly with each provider. The company said the incident remains ongoing.

The breach lands amid a run of AI-enabled cyber incidents. Earlier this month, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike said a China-based hacker likely used an AI penetration-testing agent, which probes computer systems for weaknesses, and Claude in attacks on South Korean banks. Last week, India’s cybersecurity agency warned that AI agents, including some being tested by AI companies, had reached Indian organizations’ systems without authorization.

Anthropic 和谷歌都封锁了他们认为已暴露的 API 密钥，而 OpenAI 表示，它与 OpenCode 合作恢复了访问权限，并向其 API 客户退还了攻击中使用的积分。 OpenCode 表示正在对未经授权的费用进行退款。
暴露的密钥仅限于控制台，一些用户将它们放在工作区中。联合创始人 Dax Raad 表示，开源应用程序和命令行工具没有受到影响。 “请注意，这是 OpenCode 控制台，而不是 OpenCode 本身，这些密钥永远不会传给我们，”他在 X 上写道。
即使用户和人工智能公司采取行动禁用暴露的密钥，OpenCode 团队仍然面临压力。 Raad 表示，攻击者在 48 小时内一直试图不间断地闯入其系统，要求团队保持 AI 防御代理全天候运行。 OpenCode 团队用来进行分析的人工智能模型在一段时间内起到了一定作用，但当他们被要求检查激活的安全过滤器的恶意代码时，它开始拒绝工作。
“这有点令人沮丧，”他在 X 上写道。
OpenCode 后来获得了 OpenAI 的 Daybreak Blue 计划的访问权限，该计划为经过审查的用户提供了不太可能拒绝防御安全工作请求的 AI 模型。拉德表示，此次访问提高了团队调查攻击的能力。
OpenCode 并不是第一家遇到这堵墙的公司。今年 7 月，人工智能平台 Hugging Face 表示，商业人工智能模型阻止了其分析自主人工智能代理入侵的活动日志的尝试，OpenAI 后来透露，这是其自己的模型，在测试期间降低了安全措施。 Hugging Face 在其博客文章标题为“不对称问题”的部分中写道，护栏“无法区分事件响应者和攻击者”。
安全研究人员也提出了类似的抱怨，称这些限制不一致，并迫使一些人转向任何人都可以下载和运行的外国开放权重模型。
周末的节目引起了总统科学技术顾问委员会联合主席戴维·萨克斯的回应。
“OpenCode（和早期的 Hugging Face）在攻击中遇到了同样的问题：前沿模型拒绝分析防御所需的漏洞，因为有效载荷触发了安全过滤器。护栏适得其反，”他在 X 上写道。
该漏洞发生在 OpenCode 向用户免费提供 GLM-5.3-Flash 的同一天晚上。更广泛的 GLM-5.3 系列引起了研究开放权重模型的研究人员的关注，并指出其网络安全功能已接近之前与 Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos Preview 等限制访问模型相关的水平。
OpenCode 没有详细说明攻击者如何访问旧系统、如何存储密钥或任何滥用的全部范围。它已告诉受影响的用户直接向每个提供商撤销和更换密钥。该公司表示，该事件仍在继续。
此次违规事件是在一系列人工智能网络事件中发生的。本月早些时候，网络安全公司 CrowdStrike 表示，一名中国黑客可能使用了人工智能渗透测试代理（该代理可以探测计算机系统的弱点）和克劳德（Claude）来攻击韩国银行。上周，印度网络安全机构警告称，人工智能代理，包括一些正在接受人工智能公司测试的人工智能代理，已在未经授权的情况下侵入了印度组织的系统。
